page_title: Lilo Browser: a WebKit browser for Mac with Spaces and Chrome extensions

sources.entry: Lilo - Native WebKit browser with Arc-style spaces, Chrome extensions, terminal tabs in the sidebar, and a built-in MCP server for AI agents. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Alexays/Lilo) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Lilo Browser
summary.one_liner: Lilo is a free, open-source, private-by-default Mac web browser built on Apple's WebKit engine (not Chromium) that runs Chrome Web Store extensions, offers Arc-style Spaces and sidebar terminal tabs, and includes a built-in MCP server for AI agents.
use_cases: private everyday web browsing on a Mac
giving AI agents a real browser to control
keeping work and personal sign-ins separate
browsing with a terminal and localhost beside docs
summary.what_it_does: Lilo is a native macOS browser written in Swift on top of the WebKit engine that ships with macOS, with no Chromium or Electron bundled. It organizes browsing into Spaces, each with its own cookies, storage and extensions, and offers sidebar options such as tabs on any edge, Peek link previews, split view, and a command bar. Chrome Web Store Manifest V3 extensions install with one click, while Manifest V2 and blocking webRequest are not supported. It has terminal tabs in the sidebar on a Metal renderer, and a built-in MCP server that lets agents like Claude Code, Codex or Cursor open tabs and read pages, with approval required for sends, payments, deletions or publishing. The page states it has no account, telemetry or sync, and that ad and tracker blocking uses community filter lists.
notable: Built on WebKit with Chrome Web Store extension support (Manifest V3)
Arc-style Spaces with per-Space profiles, plus terminal tabs in the sidebar
Built-in MCP server so AI agents can drive a real browser, with approval prompts
MIT-licensed open source with no account, sync or telemetry
caveats: Mac only; requires macOS 26 or later, and no mobile app or sync
Manifest V2 extensions and blocking webRequest are unsupported; Widevine is unavailable so some streaming services play at lower quality or not at all
No offline downloads in the browser; no built-in AI, agents must be connected separately
